newsitem.title: GERMANY: Grundig seeks partner after chief ousted.
newsitem.headline: Grundig seeks partner after chief ousted.

text.p: Grundig AG chief executive Pieter van der Wal, under heavy employee pressure, resigned on Monday as the ailing electronics maker's supervisory board took control of the firm and stepped up a search for a new partner.
The board expects to name a new chief within two months as well as a business partner willing to keep Grundig production in Germany, the company said after a crisis board meeting.

The results of the search for a chief executive and partner "must lie on the table within eight weeks", supervisory board chief Christian Schwarz-Schiling said after the meeting at company headquarters in the south German town of Fuerth.

The meeting was prompted by employee furore over van der Wal's plans to cut 2,000 of Grundig's 8,500 workers and took place as hundreds of workers demonstrated for his ouster outside. Van der Wal had announced the cuts after Dutch Philips Electronics NV gave up control of Grundig on January 1.

Also on Monday, Philips said it would pull 250 million marks in capital out of Grundig in connection with the lapse of its contract to run the company, which lost 250 million marks ($153 million) in 1996 and 600 million in 1995.
But Schwarz-Schilling said Grundig had questions about the legality of the move. "A clear legal analysis about who had the right to do this is required," he said.

Philips owns 32 percent of Grundig and ran the company under a contract with the Max Grundig Foundaiton, which holds a stake of almost 70 percent. Philips said it planned to keep its stake as a passive shareholder.

While seeking a new partner over the next two months, Grunding will not sell off any businesses, said the IG Metall union, which presented the supervisory board with signatures of 2,000 workers demanding a new managing director.

Van der Wal would also remain with the company for the eight weeks, although control of the company has fallen to the supervisory board since Philips has let its management contract expire, Schwarz-Schilling said.
"The management board is now solely responsible to the supervisory board," he said.
Normally under Germany's two board system, a management board handles daily operations of a company while a supervisory board oversees long-term strategy.
Grunding would seek a new chief and partner firm willing to plan a future for the company in cooperation with the board and its employees, Schwarz-Schilling said.
Van der Wal, who was hired by Philips less than a year ago, recently announced plan to move TV production to Austria and sell a video and security business.
"Philips had always promised to keep German locations, to develop the innovation potential of Grundig," Schwarz-Schilling said, adding he felt the Dutch company had failed to keep its word.
Grundig also said P.M. de Jong, a Bahlsen KG executive who had previously worked at Grundig, would succeed Karl Heinz Wieland as finance chief. Wieland resigned on January 13.
Stefan Kobold would become top marketing executive, replacing Johan van Splunter, who will step down January 31. $1=1.6285 Mark)
